FACTS_ALLOWED_IN_BODY: Toyota directs qualified technicians to inspect brake linings and drums for damage, leakage and wear and pads/discs for wear, runout and leakage.
TRW’s EPB guide requires trained professional work to OEM specifications and describes diagnostic maintenance mode and post-repair calibration for its covered systems.
HELLA describes different EPB architectures in its Audi A8 and BMW 7 Series examples, showing why the fitted system and repair procedure need identification.
Tesla says the owner is responsible for maintenance-summary accuracy, including independent and DIY work, and restricts brake-fluid-level checking to Tesla or professional repair shops.
Tesla notes regenerative braking can mean less frequent friction-pad use while rust and corrosion may still accumulate; it calls for periodic visual inspection with wheels removed.
Brembo lists minimum-thickness, scoring, cracking, surface discoloration and deformation as inspection concerns; the relevant manufacturer threshold matters rather than a generic thickness number.
FACTS_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_BODY: No generic pad or disc thickness, fluid interval or pass threshold
No DIY brake repair, dynamic emergency-brake test or hill test instructions
No claim that regenerative braking eliminates brake maintenance
No universal requirement that every EPB uses external scan-tool service mode
No inspection-record substitute for competent physical inspection
